text:
anna: FYI audit ping: a handful of snapshot objects in prod lack tenant CMEK tags. Looks like uploader didn't attach `x-amz-meta-cmek-id`.

devin: Is that the new multipart uploader we rolled last week?

anna: Yep, archiver-multipart v3.0. On retries the code path uses a fresh part request and our metadata map isn't copied into the retry request. Repro log: 

[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] ERROR part upload failed, scheduling retry
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] DEBUG building retry request headers = { Authorization, Content-Length }
[2026-03-21T09:12:01Z] DEBUG metadata on request = {}

lee: Are objects actually unencrypted or using bucket SSE fallback?

anna: Bucket policy enforces SSE, so they're server-side encrypted with platform key, not tenant CMEK. Compliance risk for customers with CMEK requirement.

maya: Any recent IAM/RBAC changes for archiver service account? We trimmed its policy during the roles cleanup.

devin: I recall removing kms:Encrypt for that SA and gating encrypt calls behind a feature flag. If it can't call KMS we should still set metadata and let the bucket reject upload if needed, not silently drop CMEK tag.

anna: Exactly. Current behavior: when KMS call fails, uploader falls back to copy-without-cmek. That's the bug.

encops-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-157 "archiver-cmek-metadata-omission". Priority: P1. Assigned: @oncall.

oncall: Acknowledged. Starting mitigation: 1) revert recent role tightening for archiver-sa, 2) hotfix to ensure metadata survives retry path, 3) run object audit to enumerate affected keys.

devin: For enumeration use prefix scanning + head-object to check metadata header. Example: 

python3 check_meta.py --bucket snapshots-prod --prefix "db/" --after 2026-03-20T00:00Z > /tmp/missing_cmek.txt

# check_meta uses boto3.HeadObject and inspects Metadata.get('cmek-id')

lee: Remediation options? Re-wrap with KMS via copy or ask customers to re-run backups. Re-wrapping could be done in-bucket by object copy with `--metadata-directive REPLACE` and `--sse aws:kms`.

maya: Need to confirm KMS grants for archiver-sa include: kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:Encrypt, kms:DescribeKey. If not, re-wrap will fail.

anna: I'll validate IAM and push RBAC rollback if needed. Timeline: RBAC rollback in 10m, hotfix PR in 90m, audit run in 3h.

devin: Add tests: multipart retry system test, and a tiny e2e that simulates KMS failure -> ensure upload fails rather than silently stripping metadata. Also add a prometheus metric `archiver.cmek_attach_failures` and an alert rule (pager) if > 5/min.

oncall: RBAC rollback complete — archiver-sa policy restored. Verified `kms:GenerateDataKey` present. Ran a quick upload, got cmek-id metadata attached.

anna: Starting re-wrap job for affected keys. I'll use lambda-run with concurrency limit 10 to avoid bursting S3. Script snippet: 

aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket snapshots-prod --prefix "db/2026-03-20/" --query "Contents[].Key" --output text | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} aws s3 cp s3://snapshots-prod/{} s3://snapshots-prod/{} --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:region:acct:key/xxxx

maya: Notify Compliance + Support. Prepare templated message for tenants whose snapshots were affected. Include remediation steps and timeline.

devin: Add a post-deploy check that scans the last 48h and pages SRE if any object lacking cmek metadata is found.

anna: Will open the hotfix PR (fix: preserve metadata on multipart retry) and link the tests. Postmortem draft ETA EOD.

lee: Good. Also let's ensure the uploader logs include request metadata snapshot when debug is on to speed future triage.

oncall: All mitigation actions done. Continuing re-wrap job and monitoring. Will update incident with counts once audit completes.

maya: Thanks team. Please keep the compliance lead in loop. :pray:
